heroLead: Central Lake sits in the middle of Antrim County's Chain of Lakes, and the farmland ringing those lakes carries some of the county's more consistent Antrim Shale production.
intro: Central Lake is a small village on the lake of the same name, connected into Antrim County's larger Chain of Lakes system, with farm and orchard land surrounding it that saw genuine Antrim Shale drilling activity during the late 1980s and 1990s boom. If your family has held land in this area, a mineral interest tied to it is very plausibly connected to a well that's been producing, slowly and steadily, for three decades or more.

sections.heading: Farmland and orchard country with real well density
paragraphs: This part of Antrim County saw fairly tight well spacing during the boom years, meaning if your family owned land around Central Lake through the late 1980s and 1990s, there's a real chance a lease was signed and a well drilled nearby, whether or not anyone in the current generation remembers it happening.
We check current production and recent statements against your specific section before quoting anything, since not every parcel that got leased in this area actually got drilled.

sections.heading: What ownership and value look like now
paragraphs: Mineral ownership around Central Lake commonly traces through family farms held across generations, sometimes split from the surface, sometimes still attached to it. Where there's active production, it's decades into a mature, low-decline stage, meaning modest but steady checks rather than anything resembling the well's early years. We'll give you the honest number based on your actual statements, not a guess pulled from what the area did at its peak.

sections.heading: What we need to evaluate a Central Lake interest
paragraphs: Send your deed or probate document, any royalty statements or division orders you've received, and the legal description if you have it. Given the density of drilling in this part of the county, we're often able to identify the well tied to your interest quickly once we have the section, township, and range.
If several family members share the interest, note that too. It's common near Central Lake for one original lease to have been split among multiple heirs over the years.

faqs.question: Is there significant Antrim Shale production around Central Lake?
faqs.answer: Yes, this part of Antrim County saw real drilling density during the boom years, though we still check your specific section since not every leased parcel was drilled.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my Central Lake area land was ever leased?
faqs.answer: The Antrim County register of deeds in Bellaire holds recorded leases and deeds for parcels throughout the county, including the Central Lake area.

faqs.question: Why does my royalty check from a Central Lake well seem small now?
faqs.answer: Wells from this area's 1990s boom are decades into a long, flat decline, which means smaller, steadier volumes and smaller checks than the well's early production years.

faqs.question: Can I sell my share of a Central Lake mineral interest if I only own a fraction of it?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally each owner can sell their own fractional share independently, whether that share is a half, a quarter, or a much smaller inherited piece.
